Subject: Initial capacity alignment for Moirai commit

Hi Ethan / Samantha,

Congrats again on getting approval from your exec team — excited to get Moirai onto Dedicated. Before we lock final sizing in the contract, can you confirm the expected production profile for the first 90 days? Specifically:

- Peak concurrent requests and target p99 latency (50/100/200 token windows)
- Expected daily token volume and steady-state concurrency
- Batchable vs interactive endpoints (what % can be batched)
- Any IP/region constraints (we have US-east and EU-west pools)

I attached our suggested sizing worksheet (moirai_sizing_v3.xlsx) — if you can fill the highlighted cells we’ll run a quick fit check on our side and propose a provisional node anchoring to hold capacity during legal.

Next steps I propose: you fill the sheet by Mon, Jul 31; we run ops sizing and confirm a 14-day provisional hold. If that timeline works, I’ll loop in Marissa and Karthik for the internal check.

Thanks —
Olga

Hi Olga —

Thanks, Olga. Quick answers inline:

- Peak concurrent: ~120 concurrent users during business hours; p99 target 250ms on 100-token window.
- Daily token volume: 1.8M tokens/day expected initially, ramping to ~4M over 3 months.
- Batchable: ~60% of inference is background batch; 40% interactive.
- Region: US-east only for launch (can expand later).

I filled the key fields in the sheet and attached it. We’re targeting production cutover mid-August — legal is in final review. The hold sounds good. Can you confirm what a 14-day provisional hold means operationally (is it capacity reserved, billed, etc.)?

Appreciate it —

- Flag any hard blockers (eviction risk, GPU shortages in the August window, thermal packing constraints).

If you can get me an ops note by EOD Tue (Jul 31 PST) I’ll pull together a short note for Sales/Legal.

Thanks —
Olga

Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial capacity alignment for Moirai commit — ops sizing request

Olga —

TL;DR: We can provision a provisional anchor that covers Moirai’s initial runway with the following specifics. Full note below.

Proposed provisional anchor (14 days):
- Reserve: 12 slots on Dedicated-us-east pool mapped to 8xA100-40GB equivalent (logical shard configuration to support 120 concurrent + 60% batched workload headroom).
- Billing: provisional hold is a zero-charge reservation for 14 days; billing triggers on contract activation or if customer requests early activation. If contract does not finalize after 14 days we release the slots automatically.
- Ops limits: no hard eviction during hold but nodes are flagged for soft-fallback (if insufficient capacity for higher-priority enterprise commitments we will notify 72 hours ahead).
- Thermal/packing: current staging shows 18% thermal headroom in us-east; we recommend staggered start to avoid initial throttles.

Fit notes:
- 1.8M -> 4M tokens/day maps to ~9k-20k tokens/sec average depending on traffic shape. Given their batch ratio and target p99, 12 slots (8xA100-eq) gives 1.2x safety margin for first 30 days; recommend reevaluation at day 21 of the hold.
- If Moirai wants a safer buffer, 16 slots would give ~1.6x margin; ops preference is 12 now and plan to spin additional nodes within 48h if ramp requires.

Attachments: redwood_capacity_manifest.pdf (contains current us-east node inventory and provisional hold id: HOLD-2028-7984)

Next steps I suggest:
1) Olga confirm provisional hold id to share with Moirai (HOLD-2028-7984 exists but not yet committed).
2) Legal to accept provisional wording (I can add short ops SLA language).
3) We set an internal 21-day check cadence to validate telemetry once live.

Marissa
